method_definitions.avg_cap: McMaster & Wilhelm (1997) Method 2: reset Tmin/Tmax below tbase to tbase and Tmax above tupper to tupper before averaging; GDD = (Tmax+Tmin)/2 - tbase.
method_definitions.avg: McMaster & Wilhelm (1997) Method 2 with the tbase floor only (no upper cap).

Corn (maize).source: McMaster & Wilhelm 1997 Agric For Meteorol 87:291-300; NDAWN corn GDD

Soybean.source: NDAWN soybean GDD (corn thresholds); OK Mesonet uses 10/35
Soybean.notes: Published models use Tbase 7-14 and Tupper 30-45; 10/30 is operational standard.

Spring wheat.source: NDAWN wheat GDD (Bauer et al. 1984); Miller et al. 2001 MSU MT200103AG; McMaster & Wilhelm 1997
Spring wheat.notes: NDAWN caps Tmax at 21 C before Haun 2.0 (~395 GDD) and 35 C after; stage-dependent cap not encoded.

Winter wheat.source: McMaster & Wilhelm 1997; OK Mesonet (0/30); KSU MF3740 (0/26)

Durum wheat.source: Treated as wheat: NDAWN wheat GDD; MSU MT200103AG
Durum wheat.notes: No durum-specific base found; NDAWN model fitted on hard red spring wheat.

Barley.source: NDAWN barley GDD (Bauer et al. 1992); MSU MT200103AG
Barley.notes: NDAWN stage caps 21 C (pre Haun 2.0, 384 GDD) then 35 C.

Oat.source: MSU MT200103AG (0 C); Mohammed Yusoff et al. 2013 Crop Pasture Sci 63:1097 (1.6 emergence, 3.0 leaf)

Canola.source: NDAWN canola GDD (41 F); MSU and Canola Council use 0 C
Canola.notes: Range 0-5 C; emergence base 0.4-1.2 C (Vigil et al. 1997). Use 0 C to reproduce MSU/Canola Council tables.

Pea (field pea).source: Miller, Lanier & Brandt 2001 MSU MT200103AG Table 1

Lentil.source: MSU MT200103AG Table 1; Safahani et al. 2017 Legume Res 40:291 (emergence Tb 4.5)
Lentil.notes: Whole-season phenology work uses 0 C; emergence-only base 4.5 C.

Chickpea.source: MSU MT200103AG Table 1 (desi); NZ kabuli phenology base 1 C

Dry bean.source: HPRCC/AWDN dry bean crop file (50/86 F)
Dry bean.notes: Brazilian studies test 10-15 C; no NDAWN dry-bean page found.

Sunflower.source: NDAWN sunflower GDD (44 F, no upper threshold identified)
Sunflower.notes: MSU uses 0 C; KSU 7.8/30; genotype bases 3.9-9.7 C.

Sorghum.source: Univ. Arkansas MP297 Grain Sorghum Handbook ch.1 (50/100 F); KSU Mesonet

Cotton.source: OSU PSS-3002 DD60 (base 60 F); cap 95 F per KSU MF3740 / Texas A&M
Cotton.notes: Tbase high confidence; cap varies 93-100 F or none.

Potato.source: Sands, Hackett & Nix 1979 Field Crops Res 2:309-331 (via FSHS 118); Manitoba Agriculture heat units page (7/21/30 C)
Potato.notes: P-days (Sands) are a nonlinear alternative; HPRCC uses 45/97 F.

Sugar beet.source: NDAWN sugarbeet GDD (34/86 F); Milford et al. 1985 Ann Appl Biol 106:163 use 3 C
Sugar beet.notes: Use 3 C / no cap when coupling to European beet models.

Alfalfa.source: Penn State Extension Understanding GDD (41 F); OK Mesonet (41/86 F)
Alfalfa.notes: KSU MF3740 lists 0/30 C. GDD mainly used for first cutting.

Rice.source: Univ. Arkansas FSA-2124 DD50 program (base 50 F, Tmax cap 94 F)
Rice.notes: DD50 also sets Tmin = 70 F when Tmin > 70 F (max 32 DD50/day); not encoded.

Hemp.source: Lisson, Mendham & Carberry 2000 Aust J Exp Agric 40:405-411
Hemp.notes: Phase-specific estimates 1.4-6.2 C; germination 3.4 C (Geneve); US trials report base 10 C.

Camelina.source: Allen, Vigil & Jabro 2014 Agron J 106:940-944 (emergence Tb -0.70 C)
Camelina.notes: Rounded from -0.7 (Allen) and ~0.5 (Sintim 2015 abstract); emergence-based only.

Safflower.source: Torabi, Adibniya & Rahimi 2015 Int J Plant Prod 9:393-412 (emergence Tb 3.4, Topt 22, Tceil 35)
Safflower.notes: Emergence-based; crop models commonly use 5 C.

Millet.source: UNL CropWatch proso millet trial reports (base 50 F); pearl millet planting-date studies (base 10 C)
Millet.notes: Pearl millet germination/emergence bases 8-15.5 C; no proso-specific cardinal study found.

Peanut.source: UF/IFAS AE428 (Tbase 56 F); OK Mesonet (55/95 F); NCSU DD56 with 95 F ceiling
Peanut.notes: AgroClimate default cap 86 F; maturity ~2500 DD56.

Faba bean.source: Mohammed Yusoff et al. 2013 Crop Pasture Sci 63:1097-1105 (emergence Tb 1.2, leaf appearance 2.4)
Faba bean.notes: Subperiod bases 2.1-4.5 C (Confalone); 0 C by analogy with other cool-season pulses.

Mustard.source: MSU MT200103AG Table 1 (B. juncea and S. alba)
Mustard.notes: Use 5 C if treated like canola (NDAWN).

Triticale.source: Naylor & Su 1998 J Agric Sci (thermal time above 0 C); small-grain convention

Rye.source: Mirsky et al. 2009 Agron J 101:1589-1596 (rye phenology model, base 4.4 C)
Rye.notes: Small-grain networks use 0 C; chamber study gives -4.5 C. Use 0 C for consistency with wheat/barley if preferred.
